transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I just don’t really feel happy or close to people anymore. Even when my wife tries to get us back into our old Sunday routines, or something goes well at work, I know I should feel good, but I just… don’t. It feels flat.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Since the retrofit accident… so, about a year and seven months now. It’s been pretty much like this since then.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before the accident?

Not really, no. I still do some of the things I used to, like the Sunday stuff with my wife, but it doesn’t feel the same. I don’t get much enjoyment out of it, and even when something good happens at work, I don’t really feel happy about it. It just feels kind of empty.
Have you had any periods in the last year and seven months where you felt really down or depressed, separate from the general flat feeling you described?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say there was a separate stretch where I felt depressed in a different way. It’s more been this same flat, disconnected feeling most of the time.
Do you still have interest in activities or have you lost interest in things you used to like?

I’ve lost a lot of interest, yeah. I still go along with some things, like the Sunday routines with my wife, but I don’t really feel happy or close the way I used to. Even when something goes well at work, I just don’t get that good feeling from it anymore.
Have you had any periods where you felt extremely sad or depressed?
I don’t think so, not in the sense of a clear period where I was extremely sad. It’s more like I’ve felt flat and disconnected most of the time, rather than having a separate depressed spell.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since you started feeling this way?
Not that I’ve really noticed. My weight seems about the same, maybe a little up or down here and there, but nothing significant.
Have you had any other periods in your life before the accident where you felt similarly flat and disconnected?

No, not really. Before the accident I had normal ups and downs, but I could still feel happy, feel close to my wife, enjoy our Sunday routines, and feel good when something went well at work. Since then it’s like that part is just... not there the same way.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the accident?

Yes. I feel on edge a lot. On the floor I’m constantly checking the gauges, the exits, people’s hands, where the emergency stops are. Even in meetings, I’ll choose a seat where I can see the door. It’s like I can’t just sit and trust things are okay.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this way in your life before the accident?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had rough patches like anyone, but not feeling like this before the accident.
Have you had other times in your life before the accident when you felt depressed or really down for a while?
Not that I can think of. I mean, I’ve had stressful times before, and bad days, but I don’t remember ever being really down for a stretch like this before the accident.
Have you ever felt this low or disconnected from people and activities before the accident and then gotten better on your own or with help?
No, not really. I don’t remember ever feeling this low or cut off from people before the accident and then having it pass. This feels different from anything I dealt with before.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really. I mean, my wife tries to get me to do our old Sunday routines, things I used to like, but I don’t feel much from it. Even if something goes well at work, I know I should feel good, but I just… don’t really feel happy or close to anyone like I used to.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this flat and disconnected since the accident?

Yes. It’s happened more than once since the accident. I’ll have stretches where I just feel flat, like I can’t really feel happiness or closeness. Even when my wife tries to get me into our old Sunday routines, or something goes well at work, I know I should feel something, but I don’t.
How long have you been feeling flat and disconnected this time?
It’s been going on pretty much since the retrofit accident… so about a year and seven months now.
Did you ever feel depressed for a long period before the accident?
Not that I can really remember. I had rough patches like anyone, but nothing that lasted a long time like this before the accident.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy before the accident but no longer find pleasure in?

Yeah. The big one is our Sunday routine with my wife. We used to have coffee, maybe take a walk, just spend time together, and I’d actually enjoy it. Now I go through the motions, but I don’t feel much—no real happiness or closeness. Even when something goes well at work, it just doesn’t land the way it used to.
Is this the only time since the accident that you've felt this flat and disconnected, or have you had other episodes like this that have gone away and then come back?

It hasn’t really gone away and come back. It’s been pretty constant. What brings me in is that I just don’t feel real happiness or closeness anymore, even when my wife tries to do our old Sunday routine with me, or when something goes well at work. It just doesn’t reach me like it used to.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you felt normal and not flat or disconnected since the accident?

No, not really. I can’t think of any stretch that long where I felt like myself again. What brings me in is that I still don’t feel real happiness or closeness, even with the Sunday stuff my wife tries to do, or when something at work goes well. It’s just… flat.
Have you had at least two months without feeling flat or disconnected from people and activities since the accident?

No, I haven’t had a two-month stretch like that. It’s been pretty steady—what brings me in is I just don’t feel real happiness or closeness anymore, even when my wife tries to get me into our old Sunday routine or something good happens at work. It just doesn’t really get through.
